title: 2 Kings 15: The Kings of a Divided House
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Kings 15](/bible/2-kings/15)

This session covers [2 Kings 15](/bible/2-kings/15) through 18. It follows the fast turnover of kings in Israel, marked by conspiracy and murder, while Judah's kings walk in mixed obedience. It moves through the rise of Assyria against the land, the idolatry of Ahaz, the carrying away of Israel into captivity for breaking the covenant, and the reforms of Hezekiah as Assyria begins to posture against Judah. The thread throughout is that the Most High keeps His word: He blesses those who keep His commandments and delivers into the hand of spoilers those who forsake them.

**[2 Kings 15:1-7](/bible/2-kings/15#v1)**
> <sup>[1](/bible/2-kings/15#v1)</sup> In the twenty and seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel began Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah to reign.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-kings/15#v2)</sup> Sixteen years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned two and fifty years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Jecholiah of Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-kings/15#v3)</sup> And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Amaziah had done;
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/2-kings/15#v4)</sup> Save that the high places were not removed: the people sacrificed and burnt incense still on the high places.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-kings/15#v5)</sup> And the Lord smote the king, so that he was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house. And Jotham the king’s son was over the house, judging the people of the land.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-kings/15#v6)</sup> And the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-kings/15#v7)</sup> So Azariah slept with his fathers; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Jotham his son reigned in his stead.

- Azariah, also called Uzziah, begins to reign over Judah and does that which is right in the sight of the Most High as his father Amaziah had done.
- The high places were not removed, so the people still sacrificed and burned incense there, an incomplete obedience.
- The Most High smote him so that he was a leper until his death, and he dwelt in a separate house while Jotham his son judged the people.
- Azariah's fuller history is written elsewhere, and the teacher directs the reader to [2 Chronicles 26](/bible/2-chronicles/26) for a more detailed account of his life and acts.
  - **[2 Chronicles 26:1](/bible/2-chronicles/26#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/2-chronicles/26#v1)</sup> Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah.

    Azariah is named Uzziah, the same king given in greater detail in Chronicles.

**[2 Kings 15:8-12](/bible/2-kings/15#v8)**
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-kings/15#v8)</sup> In the thirty and eighth year of Azariah king of Judah did Zachariah the son of Jeroboam reign over Israel in Samaria six months.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/2-kings/15#v9)</sup> And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his fathers had done: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-kings/15#v10)</sup> And Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-kings/15#v11)</sup> And the rest of the acts of Zachariah, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-kings/15#v12)</sup> This was the word of the Lord which he spake unto Jehu, saying, Thy sons shall sit on the throne of Israel unto the fourth generation. And so it came to pass.

- Zachariah son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel only six months and does that which is evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam.
- Shallum conspires against Zachariah, smites him before the people, slays him, and reigns in his place.
- The end of Zachariah fulfills the word spoken to Jehu, that his sons would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.
  - **[2 Kings 10:30](/bible/2-kings/10#v30)**
    > <sup>[30](/bible/2-kings/10#v30)</sup> And the Lord said unto Jehu, Because thou hast done well in executing that which is right in mine eyes, and hast done unto the house of Ahab according to all that was in mine heart, thy children of the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.

    The Most High promised Jehu that his children of the fourth generation would sit on Israel's throne, fulfilled in Zachariah.

**[2 Kings 15:13-16](/bible/2-kings/15#v13)**
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-kings/15#v13)</sup> Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the nine and thirtieth year of Uzziah king of Judah; and he reigned a full month in Samaria.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-kings/15#v14)</sup> For Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, and came to Samaria, and smote Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, and slew him, and reigned in his stead.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-kings/15#v15)</sup> And the rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he made, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-kings/15#v16)</sup> Then Menahem smote Tiphsah, and all that were therein, and the coasts thereof from Tirzah: because they opened not to him, therefore he smote it; and all the women therein that were with child he ripped up.

- Shallum reigns a full month in Samaria before Menahem son of Gadi goes up from Tirzah, smites him, and reigns in his stead.
- Menahem strikes Tiphsah and its coasts because they would not open to him, and he ripped up the women with child, a mark of his cruelty.

**[2 Kings 15:17-22](/bible/2-kings/15#v17)**
> <sup>[17](/bible/2-kings/15#v17)</sup> In the nine and thirtieth year of Azariah king of Judah began Menahem the son of Gadi to reign over Israel, and reigned ten years in Samaria.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-kings/15#v18)</sup> And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not all his days from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-kings/15#v19)</sup> And Pul the king of Assyria came against the land: and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-kings/15#v20)</sup> And Menahem exacted the money of Israel, even of all the mighty men of wealth, of each man fifty shekels of silver, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back, and stayed not there in the land.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-kings/15#v21)</sup> And the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/2-kings/15#v22)</sup> And Menahem slept with his fathers; and Pekahiah his son reigned in his stead.

- Menahem reigns ten years in Samaria and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam.
- Pul the king of Assyria comes against the land, and Menahem gives him a thousand talents of silver to confirm the kingdom in his hand.
- Menahem raises the tribute by exacting fifty shekels of silver from each mighty man of wealth, so the king of Assyria turns back and does not stay in the land.

**[2 Kings 15:23-26](/bible/2-kings/15#v23)**
> <sup>[23](/bible/2-kings/15#v23)</sup> In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah Pekahiah the son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned two years.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/2-kings/15#v24)</sup> And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/2-kings/15#v25)</sup> But Pekah the son of Remaliah, a captain of his, conspired against him, and smote him in Samaria, in the palace of the king’s house, with Argob and Arieh, and with him fifty men of the Gileadites: and he killed him, and reigned in his room.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/2-kings/15#v26)</sup> And the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

- Pekahiah son of Menahem reigns two years over Israel and does evil, not departing from the sins of Jeroboam.
- Pekah, a captain of his, conspires against him and smites him in the king's house at Samaria with fifty Gileadites, then reigns in his room.
- This is a military coup, where a trusted captain kills the king and seizes the throne.

**[2 Kings 15:27-31](/bible/2-kings/15#v27)**
> <sup>[27](/bible/2-kings/15#v27)</sup> In the two and fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and reigned twenty years.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/2-kings/15#v28)</sup> And he did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord: he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/2-kings/15#v29)</sup> In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath–pileser king of Assyria, and took Ijon, and Abel–beth–maachah, and Janoah, and Kedesh, and Hazor, and Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and carried them captive to Assyria.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/2-kings/15#v30)</sup> And Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and smote him, and slew him, and reigned in his stead, in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/2-kings/15#v31)</sup> And the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

- Pekah son of Remaliah reigns twenty years over Israel, the same Pekah spoken of in the book of Isaiah.
- In his days Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes and takes Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, carrying them captive to Assyria.
- Hoshea son of Elah conspires against Pekah, smites and slays him, and reigns in his stead.

**[2 Kings 15:32-38](/bible/2-kings/15#v32)**
> <sup>[32](/bible/2-kings/15#v32)</sup> In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel began Jotham the son of Uzziah king of Judah to reign.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/2-kings/15#v33)</sup> Five and twenty years old was he when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Jerusha, the daughter of Zadok.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/2-kings/15#v34)</sup> And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord: he did according to all that his father Uzziah had done.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/2-kings/15#v35)</sup> Howbeit the high places were not removed: the people sacrificed and burned incense still in the high places. He built the higher gate of the house of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/2-kings/15#v36)</sup> Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/2-kings/15#v37)</sup> In those days the Lord began to send against Judah Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah.
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/2-kings/15#v38)</sup> And Jotham slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Ahaz his son reigned in his stead.

- Jotham son of Uzziah reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem and does that which is right, according to all his father Uzziah had done.
- Again the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense there.
- Jotham builds the higher gate of the house of the Most High.
- In those days the Most High begins to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.
